name: Chrome extension failing silently on Edge
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person reported a frustrating issue where the Claude Code Chrome extension silently fails on Microsoft Edge — it prompts for authentication but then does nothing, while working correctly in Chrome. Claude performed a web search and provided a detailed technical explanation of the root causes.

Claude identified two likely bugs: first, that Claude Code's native messaging host is registered only under Chrome's registry path (`HKCU\SOFTWARE\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts`) and not Edge's equivalent path (`HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Edge\NativeMessagingHosts`), causing Edge to silently fail to launch the host; second, a priority-race condition involving the Claude desktop app interfering with the CLI's native host handshake. Claude provided specific Windows registry commands to diagnose which issue applies and noted that fully quitting the Claude desktop app before invoking `--chrome` is the only known workaround for the second scenario. Claude confirmed both are open, unresolved issues as of recent weeks, with no shipped fix from Anthropic, and recommended using Chrome as the more supported path in the interim.

Confirmed — this is a known issue, not something specific to your setup. Two overlapping bugs match what you're describing:

**Root cause candidates:**
1. **Native messaging host registration is Chrome-only on Windows.** Claude Code registers its native messaging host in `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts` but never writes the equivalent `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Edge\NativeMessagingHosts` key. Edge looks in its own registry path, finds nothing, and the extension just reports "not connected" with no error surfaced. The extension can be installed in Edge since it's Chromium-based, but the native messaging connection fails because Edge looks for host registrations under its own registry path, and no error is shown to the user — it simply reports the extension is not connected because the native messaging host is never launched.

2. **If you also have the Claude desktop app installed**, there's a priority-race bug where Edge's extension prefers the desktop app's native host over Claude Code's CLI host, and even when the desktop app is forced out, the CLI handshake doesn't complete — status just sits on Disabled with nothing surfaced. The extension prioritizes the desktop app's native host over the CLI's, and even when desktop is forced out of the race, the CLI's host still doesn't report Enabled — the CLI process spawns and holds a socket open, but /chrome still reports Status: Disabled with no error surfaced anywhere.

**Quick check to tell which one you're hitting** — if you're on Windows, run:
```
reg query "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Edge\NativeMessagingHosts" /s
reg query "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts" /s
```
If Chrome's key exists and Edge's is empty, that's bug #1 — Anthropic hasn't shipped the fix, and no local workaround manually adds the reg key reliably because the extension ID/manifest path Chrome uses may not match what Edge's Chromium fork expects.

If you're on Mac, or the registry checks out fine, it's more likely the desktop-app priority race (#2), in which case fully quitting the Claude desktop app before invoking `--chrome` is the only known workaround right now.

Both are open, unresolved GitHub issues as of the last few weeks — not fixed yet. If Chrome itself works fine for you, that's the more supported path until Anthropic ships the Edge registry fix.

content.title: --chrome / /chrome always shows Status: Disabled on Microsoft Edge — extension prioritizes Desktop app's native host over CLI's, and CLI host doesn't complete handshake even when it wins · Issue #79592 · anthropics/claude-code
content.text:
Even when Desktop is forced out of the race, the CLI's host still doesn't report Enabled: Renaming Desktop's native-messaging manifest (Edge-scoped only) so it can't be found forces the extension to fall through to com.anthropic.claude_code_browser_extension. When this happens, /Users/<user>/.local/bin/claude --chrome-native-host does spawn and holds a Unix socket open well past the extension's 10-second ping timeout — but /chrome still reports Status: Disabled, with no error surfaced anywhere. This suggests the CLI-side handshake (the "pong" reply, or whatever signals success back to the interactive session) isn't completing correctly, or the interactive session polling for status isn't picking up a successful connection. For business owners who'd rather build than browse. Diagnose, build, ship — with a trusted AI advisor in your back pocket.

Click the pin icon next to it to lock it into the toolbar. Chrome hides newly installed extensions by default. That does not mean the install failed. If the extension does not appear in the Extensions list at all, go to chrome://extensions in the address bar and check that the extension is enabled. Toggle it on if it is switched off. If it is missing entirely, reinstall from the Claude AI for Chrome listing on the Chrome Web Store. The extension ID in the Chrome Web Store URL is mmpfdbkbpokgghegejphmpmpnjncehip, which you can use to verify you're installing the official Anthropic build rather than a clone. 

One more thing worth checking: Edge, Arc, and Brave all support the extension and run it the same way Chrome does. If you installed it on one Chromium browser and are trying to use it in a different one, you need a separate install for each browser profile.

The most common reason the Claude Chrome extension stops working is not a broken install. It is that the extension was never granted access to the page you are on, or your account is not on a plan that supports it. Most people reinstall and get the same result because the root cause stays in place. I have hit every one of these failure modes building browser workflows for clients. The fix is almost never reinstalling. It is one specific permission, plan setting, or auth state that needs to be corrected. This post goes through each symptom and the exact fix.
